Koszalin New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Koszalin, Poland

Demolished. This is the newer of Koszalin's two Jewish cemeteries, established in 1901 after the older cemetery, documented elsewhere in this collection, ran out of burial space. Both necropolises were destroyed by the Germans in 1938; according to a local priest's account, tombstones were overturned and some thrown into the river, while the funeral home was burned. A 1947 survey by the Central Jewish Historical Commission found the site's oldest monuments dated to 1900, made of polished granite with Hebrew and German inscriptions. The Koszalin University of Technology now stands on the site; a memorial was unveiled there in 2006 through the efforts of university researchers working with a local priest and photographer.
